beats.say: In twenty twenty-four, India imported a hundred and sixty thousand tonnes of used clothes.
Over half came from the US.
Many end up in Panipat, ninety kilometres north of Delhi.
Its nickname is the cast-off capital.
Why here? Panipat was already the City of Weavers, full of mills.
Customs makes sure they're slashed first, so no one can wear them again.
beats.cap: Cut up at customs. Can't be worn.

beats.say: Then they're sorted by colour, shredded into fibre, and spun into yarn.
It's an old English method, called shoddy.
So the world's old clothes come back as blankets, many for refugee camps.
